title: Getting Started
summary: Learn how to sign in and use the menu.

sections.title: Before you begin
paragraphs: Ask your manager for your work login and the modules you should use. The screen can hide actions your account cannot perform.

sections.title: Sign in
paragraphs: 1. Open the WATCON application.
2. Enter Email or username and Password.
3. Click Sign in.
4. If asked, enter Current password, New password and Confirm new password. Click Update password.

sections.title: Find your work
paragraphs: Use the left menu on a desktop. On a phone, use the navigation button at the top. Open Tasks for your assigned work. Open a record to see its details.

sections.title: Save safely
paragraphs: Check the project, party, item, brand, quantity and date before saving. A draft changes totals only once it is finalized, confirmed or issued. Wait for confirmation before trying again.

sections.title: Sign out
paragraphs: Open your account menu and choose Sign out. Do this on shared computers.

sections.title: Verification note
paragraphs: This guide explains the available screens. Use only actions your account allows. Ask your supervisor when a business rule is unclear. Training screenshots use fictional records.

sections.title: How to get a manual
paragraphs: Help & User Guide is available to Super Admin in Administration → Help & guide. Other employees should ask their supervisor or Super Admin for a copy of this manual. Help pages and downloads are restricted to Super Admin.

sections.title: What happens after saving?
paragraphs: Read the saved status. Draft records still need the next action described above. A draft changes nothing until you finalize, confirm or issue it.

sections.title: Does it affect stock or accounts?
paragraphs: Viewing this page does not post stock or money. Totals follow your permissions.

sections.title: What should I do next?
paragraphs: Open the record that needs attention.

sections.title: Common mistakes to avoid
paragraphs: Do not use another project, brand or party just to make a form save. Do not enter the same physical movement twice. Ask your supervisor before cancelling or reversing a posted record.

sections.title: Check work before billing
paragraphs: Material becomes billable as soon as its site challan is dispatched — the bill does not wait for the site to confirm receipt. If the site later records damage or a shortage (returned or written off), that quantity is deducted on the next bill. If nothing more of that material is dispatched, a GST credit note (quantity × order rate + GST) is raised and applied automatically when the final bill is invoiced — against the final invoice first, then the order's other unpaid invoices. The final bill shows it and takes it off the total payable. The final bill must still bill something (e.g. installation); otherwise raise the credit note from Credit / debit notes. Material that leaves the site again (returns, transfers) is deducted too. The order quantity is always the upper limit.

title: Complete Business Workflow
summary: Follow material and money from project setup to settlement.

sections.title: Project and tasks
paragraphs: Projects → Team Members and Departments → Tasks → progress updates → project review.

sections.title: Procurement
paragraphs: Material Planning → Requisitions → Rate Enquiries → Purchase Orders → Site receipts → Supplier Bills → Payments & Receipts.

sections.title: Sales and billing
paragraphs: Clients → Client POs or Quotations → Sales Orders → Challans → Running Bills → Client Invoices → Payments & Receipts → Project Accounts.

sections.title: Partial work and returns
paragraphs: Record only quantities actually received, dispatched or measured. Use separate receipts or bills for later quantities. Keep references linked. Use the available reversal or cancellation actions; never erase historical transactions.

sections.title: Stock rule
paragraphs: PO and SO drafts or approvals do not move stock. Supplier GRN posting adds accepted quantities. Challan dispatch moves stock out of the source; internal receipts move transit stock to destination. Supplier bill approval does not add stock in this version.

sections.title: Fictional training example
paragraphs: Use only the isolated test application. Project: ABC Hotel Swimming Pool Installation. Client: ABC Hotel Training. Supplier: Training Pool Supplies. Material: Pool filter, Training brand, unit Nos.
Purchase 10 filters at ₹1,000 each. With 18% GST and no discount or charges, taxable value is ₹10,000, GST ₹1,800 and bill total ₹11,800. Same-state GST is CGST ₹900 plus SGST ₹900.

Receive 6 filters and then 4. After both supplier GRNs are posted, stock rises by 10. Record the supplier bill for ₹11,800. Stock stays at 10. Pay ₹5,000 and then ₹6,800, allocating both payments. Supplier due becomes zero.

Agree a client order for 10 filters at ₹1,500 each. Taxable value is ₹15,000, GST ₹2,700 and total ₹17,700. Deliver 4 and then 6 through client-delivery challans. Stock falls first to 6, then to zero.

Prepare the eligible running bills and record client certification. Issue matching Client Invoices. Receive ₹7,080 and then ₹10,620 with allocations. Final client due is zero. For this example use no retention, advance recovery, TDS or other deductions.

Expected material margin is ₹5,000 before labour and overheads, excluding GST. Verify project accounts, all tasks and outstanding documents before project closure. This numerical example is a training worksheet; the audit evidence states which workflows were actually executed.

sections.title: Practical training in 19 steps
paragraphs: Use an isolated training application. The trainer needs the required permissions. Records are finalized by the person who prepares them; Admins can amend or cancel final records with a reason, and only Sales Order changes need the Super Admin. Never share a login.
1. Open Clients. Click Add client. Create a fictional client, or select the existing Acme Developers training record. Use the agreed test state for GST.
2. Open Projects. Click Create new project. Enter ABC Hotel Swimming Pool Installation, a fictional Site address and Project description. Choose the manager and members. Click Create project.
3. Open Team Members. Click Add member to create any missing training employees. Set their departments and temporary passwords. Existing training employees can be reused.
4. Open Tasks. Click Create task. Assign the project, departments, team members and accountable owner. Set a due date. Staff later use Update progress and comments.
5. In Items, create Training pool filter with unit Nos. In Brands, create Training brand. Link the brand from the item page. Use zero opening stock for this exercise.
6. Open Suppliers. Click Add supplier to create a fictional supplier, or use the existing Shree Cement Traders training record. Set its correct test state.
7. Open Rate Enquiries. Click New enquiry. Ask for 10 Training pool filters. Click Save enquiry. Record the supplier offer of ₹1,000 each with 18% GST and compare the offers.

8. Review the awarded Purchase Order. If the enquiry has created one, open that order instead of entering it twice. Otherwise use New purchase order. Set quantity 10, rate ₹1,000 and GST 18%. Review and press Save & finalize PO. Stock is still zero.

9. Open Site Receipts. Find the PO under Waiting to be received. Record 6 received with no damage or rejection. Upload the material photo and the supplier challan, then press Confirm receipt — stock is updated at once. Repeat for the remaining 4. Stock is now 10 at the PO receiving location.

10. Open Supplier Bills. Click Enter supplier bill and select the PO. Copy the supplier invoice reference and date. Check 10 × ₹1,000 plus GST = ₹11,800. Press Save & finalize — a bill that matches the PO and receipts is ready to pay at once. Stock remains 10.
11. Open Inventory. Check Company stock, By location and Stock ledger. Confirm the exact item, brand and receiving location. Do not enter another inward movement for the bill.

12. Open Client POs. Click New client PO. Record the client reference and the same project. Add 10 filters at ₹1,500 and 18% GST. Use zero retention and no advance recovery for this simple exercise. Save draft and obtain approval.
13. Open the Client PO and use Create sales order, or create New sales order with the contract linked. Check 10 filters at ₹1,500. Press Save & confirm order. Stock is still 10.

14. Open Challans. Use New challan and Deliver to client, with the approved Sales Order and the location that holds the filters. Save challan and Dispatch 4 filters. Repeat for the remaining 6. Keep delivery proof. Stock becomes 6, then zero.

15. Open the Sales Order and click Generate running bill. Dispatched challans fill the quantities automatically; check them and Save. Press Submit to client. A fully billed total of 10 gives ₹17,700 including GST.

16. On the running bill press Record client payment (the invoice is raised automatically). Enter ₹7,080 and save. The ₹10,620 still due is shown as previous outstanding on the next bill; record it later from the same button. Client due becomes zero. Money received before the invoice is kept as an advance; it is set against the invoice automatically when the invoice is issued (oldest advance first).
17. Open the supplier bill and use Record payment. Pay and allocate ₹5,000, then ₹6,800. Supplier due becomes zero.

18. Open Project Accounts. Check client invoiced/received ₹17,700, supplier billed/paid ₹11,800, receivable zero and payable zero. The material margin is ₹5,000 before labour and overheads. Compare the underlying records if any number differs.

19. Complete the assigned tasks. Review open orders, evidence, transit stock and all balances before closing the job. Fully delivered approved Sales Orders can move project status to Completed automatically; that status alone does not prove every bill is paid.

title: Business Terms Glossary

sections.title: Project
paragraphs: One job or work site.

sections.title: Client
paragraphs: A customer who buys materials or services from us.

sections.title: Supplier
paragraphs: A company or person we buy from.

sections.title: Item
paragraphs: A named material or product.

sections.title: Brand
paragraphs: The make of an item.

sections.title: Rate Enquiry
paragraphs: A request asking suppliers for their prices.

sections.title: Purchase Order
paragraphs: An order we send to a supplier to buy materials.

sections.title: Client Purchase Order
paragraphs: An order we receive from our client.

sections.title: Sales Order
paragraphs: Our record of the supply agreed with the client.

sections.title: Supplier Bill
paragraphs: The supplier invoice we record as money to pay.

sections.title: GRN
paragraphs: Goods Receipt Note. In this app use Site Receipts to record and post accepted arrivals.

sections.title: Challan
paragraphs: A record of materials sent, transferred or returned. It is not a tax invoice.

sections.title: Running Bill
paragraphs: A record of current and earlier measured work for review and client certification.

sections.title: Inventory
paragraphs: The material we hold and its movement history.

sections.title: Available Stock
paragraphs: Stock that can be issued from the selected location after reservations are considered.

sections.title: Advance Payment
paragraphs: Money paid or received before it is allocated to a bill or invoice.

sections.title: Outstanding Amount
paragraphs: The part of an approved bill or issued invoice still unsettled.

sections.title: Receivable
paragraphs: Money a client still owes us.

sections.title: Payable
paragraphs: Money we still owe a supplier.

sections.title: Billed Amount
paragraphs: Issued Client Invoice value in Project Accounts.

sections.title: Unbilled Amount
paragraphs: Work or supply not yet included in an issued invoice; check the specific report definition.

sections.title: Partial Payment
paragraphs: Payment of only part of the amount due.

sections.title: GST
paragraphs: Goods and Services Tax. Confirm the rate and state treatment with Accounts.

sections.title: HSN
paragraphs: The goods classification code used for tax reporting.

sections.title: Credit Adjustment
paragraphs: An approved correction that reduces the relevant amount due.

sections.title: GSTIN
paragraphs: The tax registration number of a business.

sections.title: TDS
paragraphs: Tax deducted at source. Part of a payment is withheld for tax rather than paid directly to the other party.

sections.title: PAN
paragraphs: The permanent tax account number used on official records.

sections.title: IFSC
paragraphs: The code identifying a bank branch for a transfer.

sections.title: BOQ
paragraphs: Bill of Quantities. A list of agreed work or material lines and quantities.

sections.title: Retention
paragraphs: An agreed amount the client holds back until the required stage.

sections.title: Certification
paragraphs: The client’s confirmation of the quantity or value accepted for billing.

title: Frequently Asked Questions
summary: Answers to common questions.

sections.title: Why is a menu or button missing?
paragraphs: Your role or the record status may not allow it. Ask the Super Admin to check your permissions. Do not use someone else’s login.

sections.title: Why did a PO not increase stock?
paragraphs: Orders are commitments. Stock increases when accepted supplier material is posted through Site Receipts.

sections.title: Why does my bill not increase stock?
paragraphs: This version uses GRN stock posting. A supplier bill records the amount owed and matching quantities.

sections.title: Why is company stock different from site stock?
paragraphs: Material may be in the warehouse, another site, transit or quarantine. Use By location.

sections.title: Why is payment received different from invoice settlement?
paragraphs: Part of the receipt may still be an advance. Check allocations on the receipt.

sections.title: Can I send a PDF through WhatsApp?
paragraphs: Supported task and document controls open a WhatsApp message or sharing link. Review the recipient and message. Attach a downloaded PDF manually when the control does not attach it.

sections.title: Does Project Accounts show full profit?
paragraphs: No. Its material margin excludes labour and overheads. Do not use it as a complete statutory profit statement.

sections.title: Which PDFs exist?
paragraphs: Commercial builders cover Purchase Order, Requisition, Rate Enquiry, Site Receipt, Challan, Client PO, Sales Order, client Quotation, Running Bill, Client Invoice, Supplier Bill, Payment and adjustment note. Task reports have a PDF route. A PDF option is not guaranteed for every dashboard, statement or register.

title: Troubleshooting
summary: What to do when work cannot continue.

sections.title: Sign-in problem
paragraphs: Check Email or username. Use Forgot your password? if needed. If the account is inactive, contact your administrator.

sections.title: Reset message did not arrive
paragraphs: Check your work email and spam folder. Ask the administrator to check SMTP delivery. A reset form alone does not prove email is configured.

sections.title: Insufficient stock
paragraphs: Check the exact item, brand and source location. Review reservations and receipts. Do not make a false adjustment.

sections.title: Changed by someone else
paragraphs: Refresh the record and review its latest version before trying again.

sections.title: Action refused
paragraphs: Read the reason. Your role may not have the permission. For a confirmed Sales Order, send an amendment request to the Super Admin.

sections.title: Upload problem
paragraphs: Use an allowed PDF, image, CSV or XLSX within the configured limit. SVG and executables are not accepted. Keep files free of malware.

sections.title: Network error or no confirmation
paragraphs: Reconnect and reopen the list to check whether the record saved. Avoid repeated payment entries. Tell your supervisor the reference, time and visible error; never send your password.

sections.title: Wrong totals
paragraphs: Check document statuses, project links, returns, cancellations, allocations and notes. Ask Accounts to reconcile the original records before editing anything.
